data.name: Peregrine
data.long_meaning: From the Latin word 'peregrinus', meaning 'one who travels from one place to another'. In Christian tradition, Peregrine may refer to a pilgrim or wanderer in the spiritual sense.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes a spiritual journey or pilgrimage.

in_hebrew.name: פֶּרֶגְרִין
in_hebrew.meaning: עובדה העולם בהלך חופשי, הצדיק המובהק, הגולה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: פֶּרֶגְרִין הוא כינוי לאדם העובדת בצורה שורשית, חופשית, ללא כבלי חברה, כמו שאלה הקדוש. השם נגזר מהמילה הלטינית peregrinus, שמשמעותה 'עולם', 'גולה', ו'נדוד'. במסורת הנוצרית, פֶּרֶגְרִין היה שם של קדוש, שהקדיש את חייו לעבודת אלוהים בעולם. השם נשאר כיום כשם מתייחס לאדם שעובדת עבודת אלוהים בהלך חופשי, ללא כבלי חברה.

in_greek.name: Περέγρηνος
in_greek.meaning: ἄνθρωπος τῇ ζωῇ ἐν εὐθεῖα ὁδῷ, ὁ σωτήριος, ὁ ἐξοδος
in_greek.long_meaning: Περέγρηνος (Περέγρηνος) ἐστὶ ὄνομα τοῦ ἀνθρώπου οἵτινες ζῶσιν ἐν τῇ ζωῇ ὡς ἐν εὐθεῖα ὁδῷ, ἔχοντες τὴν σωτηρίαν τῶν ἡμερῶν αὐτῶν. Ἔρχεται ἀπὸ τῆς λέξεως πέρενγκος, τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ὅστις ἔχει σωτηρίαν τῶν ἡμερῶν αὐτῶν. Ἐν τῇ ἰστορία τῆς Ἐκκλησίας, Περέγρηνος ἦν ἕνας Ἀπόστολος, ὅστις ἔπρεπε ἀπὸ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ Χριστός. Ἡ λέξη Περέγρηνος ἔχει σήμερα τὴν σημασίαν τῆς ζωῆς τῆς ἐλευθερίας, τῆς σωτηρίας, τῆς πίστεως.

in_latin.name: Peregrinus
in_latin.meaning: homo in mundo vagus, peregrinator, sanctus
in_latin.long_meaning: Peregrinus, qui significat 'homo in mundo vagus', 'peregrinator', 'sanctus'. Origine a 'peregrinari', verbale 'peregrinare' et 'peregrinari' significans 'vagari in mundo'. In Ecclesia, Peregrinus erat nomen Apostolorum, qui Christi Iesu erant. Nomen Peregrinus significat hodie libertatem vitae, salutem, fidem.

in_english.name: Peregrine
in_english.meaning: a foreigner or stranger in the world, a holy man, a wanderer
in_english.long_meaning: Peregrine is a name that signifies a person who lives a free and wandering life, a holy man or woman, a stranger in the world. The name Peregrine originates from the Latin word 'peregrinari', which means 'to roam or wander in the world'. In Christian tradition, Peregrine was the name of a saint who dedicated his life to serving God in the world. The name Peregrine remains today as a reference to a person who lives a life of freedom, faith, and service to God.

saint_reference.note: Saint Peregrine Laziosi was a 13th-century Italian saint who was known for his piety and his ability to heal others. He is the patron saint of those suffering from cancer and is often invoked for intercession in this area.

data.cultural_impact: The name Peregrine holds rich historical and cultural significance for Christians, as it is often associated with the idea of a spiritual pilgrimage or journey. In Middle Ages Europe, Peregrine was a term used for those who embarked on a journey to visit and revere religious sites and relics. The name has been passed on to various saints and martyrs who were known to have taken long and arduous journeys for their faith.
data.spiritual_significance: For Christians, the name Peregrine holds deep spiritual significance, as it represents a commitment to a lifetime journey of faith and growth. Like the physical pilgrimage of traveling to holy sites and shrines, the name reminds us of the importance of continually striving towards greater spiritual understanding and closeness to God. Peregrine is a name that encourages us to be open to new experiences, adventures, and opportunities for personal and spiritual growth, and to embrace the unknown with courage and determination.

historical_references.reference: Saint Peregrine of Africa, also known as Peregrine the African or Peregrine the Healer, was a Christian saint and martyr.
historical_references.context: Legend has it that Peregrine was a young man from Egypt who was converted to Christianity by Saint Pachomius. After being captured and taken into slavery, he was taken to Rome where he healed the sick and converted many to Christianity. He was eventually discovered and put on trial for his faith, where he was sentenced to be beaten to death with clubs. Peregrine is now the patron saint of healers, travelers, and those suffering from incurable diseases.

historical_references.reference: Peregrine Laziosi, also known as Saint Peregrine of Assisi, was an Italian layman and cleric who lived during the late 13th century.
historical_references.context: Peregrine was born into a noble family in Forlì, Italy. He lived a wild and sinful youth, but had a conversion experience after hearing a sermon by Saint Francis of Assisi. He became a hermit and then joined the Franciscan order as a lay brother. He is best known for his miraculous healing of a cancerous leg, which occurred after he prayed to Saint Francis. Peregrine is now the patron saint of cancer patients and those suffering from other diseases.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's world, the name Peregrine continues to be cherished by Christian families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Christian name websites where expectant parents research meaningful Biblical names. The name bridges traditional Christian values with modern faith identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and Biblical significance.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Sarah Peregrine in Dublin, Ireland credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Peregrine, which means "Wanderer, Pilgrim". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.

data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Peregrine symbolizes a wanderer or pilgrim in search of spiritual growth and enlightenment. It is derived from the Latin word 'peregrinus,' meaning foreigner or traveler, reflecting one's journey through life towards a deeper connection with God.
